_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: "The input" is the message input [data-testid="message-input"]; "the send button" is [data-testid="send-button"]; "queued badges" are [data-testid="queued-badge"]. "Send X and wait for work" means: fill the input with X, click the send button, and wait (up to 30s) for the thinking indicator [data-testid="agent-thinking"] to be visible. Keys pressed "in the input" go to the input while it has focus (filling it focuses it). "Press M+Enter" presses its modifiers as a keyboard does: a key_down step for each modifier M in the order written, then a press_key step "Enter" (without modifiers of its own; the held keys apply), then a key_up step for each modifier in reverse order. Every test starts: navigate to /c/queue-shortcut and wait (up to 30s) for the input to be visible. window.textCount(text) counts the innermost elements whose text contains text, ignoring case; window.textCount(text, true) counts those whose whole text is exactly text. Alt+click on Send queues the composed message. 1. Navigate to /c/queue-shortcut and wait for the input. 2. Send "delay: 60" and wait for work. 3. Fill the input with "queued via click". 4. Alt+click the send button as a user holding Alt would: a key_down step "Alt", a click on the send button with modifiers "Alt", then a key_up step "Alt". 5. The input's value should become exactly "". 6. There should be exactly one queued badge. 7. Eval window.textCount("queued via click", true) with expect "1".
